title: Number of Ways of Cutting a Pizza
statement:
A rectangular pizza is given as the string array `pizza`: row `i` is `pizza[i]`, and each cell is `'A'` (an apple) or `'.'` (nothing). You must split it into `k` pieces by making `k - 1` straight cuts, one after another, always along the grid lines of what is still left:

- A horizontal cut between two rows hands the part above the cut to a person; the part below stays.
- A vertical cut between two columns hands the part left of the cut to a person; the part to the right stays.
- After the last cut, the piece that remains goes to the last person.

Two ways are different when their sequences of cuts differ. Count the ways in which every one of the `k` pieces holds at least one apple, and return that count modulo `10^9 + 7` (return `0` if no way works).
constraints: pizza contains only the characters 'A' and '.'
notes:
## Intuition

Every cut gives away the top or the left part, so what remains is always a bottom-right corner of the pizza: it is fully described by its top-left cell `(r, c)`. The number of ways to finish depends only on that corner and on how many pieces are still needed, which makes a small DP state. Trying every sequence of cuts directly blows up exponentially.

To know quickly whether a piece holds an apple, keep suffix sums: `apples[r][c]` counts the apples in the corner starting at `(r, c)`. The strip given away by a horizontal cut at row `cut` holds `apples[r][c] - apples[cut][c]` apples, and a vertical cut at column `cut` gives away `apples[r][c] - apples[r][cut]`.

## Approach

1. Fill `apples` from the bottom-right with inclusion and exclusion.
2. One piece: `dp[r][c]` is 1 when the corner has an apple, else 0.
3. For `pieces` from 2 to `k`, build `next[r][c]`: add `dp[cut][c]` for every horizontal `cut` whose top strip has an apple, and `dp[r][cut]` for every vertical `cut` whose left strip has an apple, modulo `MOD`.
4. After `k` layers, `dp[0][0]` is the answer for the whole pizza.

## Example 1, step by step

`pizza = ["A..","AAA","..."]`, `k = 3`. Two first cuts both give away an apple and leave a corner that can still be split well: the horizontal cut at row 1 hands over `"A.."` and leaves corner `(1, 0)` = `["AAA","..."]`, and the vertical cut at column 1 hands over column 0 and leaves corner `(0, 1)`. With two pieces still needed, corner `(1, 0)` can be finished by a vertical cut at column 1 or at column 2, so its `dp` value is 2; corner `(0, 1)` only by a vertical cut at column 2, so its value is 1. The other first cuts leave corners that cannot be split into two good pieces (the cut at row 2 leaves the empty bottom row). So `dp[0][0] = 2 + 1 = 3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(k · rows · cols · (rows + cols)): each state tries every cut.
- Space: O(rows · cols) for `apples` and two DP layers.

## Pitfalls

- Check the given-away strip, not the whole corner; the remaining corner is checked by the next layer.
- Take the modulus on every addition so totals stay exact.
- A corner of a single cell cannot be cut, so asking it for more pieces gives 0.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `apples[r][c]` | apples in the corner whose top-left cell is `(r, c)` |
| `dp[r][c]` | ways to split that corner into `pieces - 1` good pieces |
| `next[r][c]` | the same for `pieces` pieces |
| `cut` | the row or column where the next cut is made |
| `total` | running count for the current corner |

narration.5: apples[r][c] will count the apples in the corner that starts at (r, c); an extra zero row and column simplify edges.
narration.6: Fill the suffix counts from the bottom row upward...
narration.9: Inclusion-exclusion: this cell plus the corner below plus the corner to the right, minus their overlap.
narration.12: With one piece left, a corner works exactly when it contains an apple.
narration.13: Add one more piece per round until k pieces are needed.
narration.15: Consider every possible remaining corner (r, c).
narration.18: Try each horizontal cut below row r.
narration.19: The strip above the cut must contain an apple.
narration.20: Then the lower corner must be split into the remaining pieces.
narration.23: Try each vertical cut right of column c.
narration.24: The strip left of the cut must contain an apple.
narration.25: Then the right corner must be split into the remaining pieces.
narration.31: This layer becomes the table for the next round.
narration.33: The whole pizza is the corner at (0, 0).
